big: A client has ₹3 lakh of long-term gain on paper in equity funds. Every year the first ₹1.25 lakh of such gain is exempt. If she does nothing, the exemption is wasted. If she realises ₹1.25 lakh and buys again, she resets her cost higher and pays no tax this year.

lines: Why sell something I want to keep?
Because the yearly exemption does not carry forward. Selling and re-buying within it lifts your cost price, so future tax is lower. It is a year-end routine, not a trade.

rows: Cost price after year 1 (₹ thousand per 100 units)
alt: Bars comparing cost price and future taxable gain with and without harvesting
caps: A client has a long-term gain of ₹1.25 lakh on paper.
She sells to use this year's exemption, then buys again.
Her cost price rises by ₹1.25 lakh, to the new price.
That gain is never taxed later. This is tax harvesting.

rows: Tax avoided later on that gain, at 12.5%
note: Rates and limits are as per current rules and change with Budgets. Confirm each year.
